site_scraper.status: AVAILABLE, NOT ANTICIPATED BY THE SPEC
site_scraper.detail: Scott's own Ultimate Web Scraper workspace ('Scott Greenwald's Workspace', Pro plan, 9947/10000 credits at preflight time). Fetches server-side, independent of this session's egress block - the only mechanism found in this session that can reach the actual target domains (CRE firm sites, trade press, EDGAR, ATS boards, network directories).
site_scraper.limitation_1_shape: Its MCP tool surface (analyze_website, scrape_pages, extract_contacts, extract_google_maps, extract_catalog, extract_shopify_store, discover_sitemap) is schema/structured-data oriented (JSON-LD, meta tags, product/contact/catalog fields). It has no generic 'clean article body text' extractor exposed to MCP - that capability ('Page Text Extractor') exists only in the product's Chrome extension, which an agent cannot drive. One test scrape_pages call against a real Matthews market-report page returned only title/meta-description/JSON-LD/breadcrumb fields - none of which contained the CoStar attribution sentence or an in-body visible date. This is a structural mismatch with the spec's core requirement to quote the exact credit sentence and derive a visible on-page date.
site_scraper.limitation_2_cost: The same single-page test consumed 51 credits, not the ~1 credit/page baseline documented in the product's own docs (search_docs: 'How Cloud Credits Work'). The docs explain why: 'The Page Unblocker uses credits on top of the per-page cost when it handles a challenge' (e.g. Cloudflare Turnstile) - real CRE firm sites likely trigger this regularly. At 51 credits/page, the 9947-credit budget caps out around ~195 page fetches, well short of the ~400+ fetches Phase One-Three would need (Source URL + Trigger Source URL per row, times 200 rows, before any retries).
